You're right, 64 bit is not enough to be really secure and is inconsistent with the OWASP web guidelines.
The 64 bit requirement is there to be compliant with [NIST 800-63b](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#71-session-bindings).
As written in the document, one of the objective of OWASP ASVS 4.0 is to minimize the number of standards and, to do so, has adopted the NIST 800-63b standard.

So either there is a modification of [the OWASP web guidelines](https://owasp.org/www-community/vulnerabilities/Insufficient_Session-ID_Length), or the recommendations deviates from each other.
